record.paper_title: Open Problems in Nuclear Density Functional Theory
record.original_question: Let Φ be a simple intrinsic nuclear state, such as a Slater determinant or Hartree-Bogoliubov state, from which rotationally projected states ΦJMK are built by angular-momentum projection. Define an intrinsic-density functional FJMK[ρ] by minimizing the projected-state energy over simple intrinsic states Φ with intrinsic density ρ; this functional depends on the allowed class of Φ and, a priori, on the angular-momentum labels J, M, and K. Under what conditions can the intrinsic state or intrinsic density be practically independent of J, M, and K so that one density ρ is valid for many projected rotational states, and how does such an intrinsic-density functional relate to the traditional three-dimensional nuclear energy density functionals used for deformed nuclei?

evidence.quote: Assume that every ΦJMK can be a good approximation to an eigenstate of H and consider the two-step minimization, EJMK = Minρ FJMK[ρ], FJMK[ρ] = MinΦ=>ρ <ΦJMK|H|ΦJMK> / <ΦJMK|ΦJMK>, where ρ is the density of Φ, and Φ is restricted to a class of simple states.
But, obviously, this DF, FJMK[ρ], depends on that subset to which Φ is restricted. Moreover, it depends on J, M, K.

But then the essentially desirable virtue of Φ would be to be practically independent of J, M, K. Can this be true? Hence the open problem : under which conditions can FJMK define just one density ρ valid for a large number of combinations JMK? How does this intrinsic DF relate [18] to the traditional three-dimensional (E)DFs used for deformed nuclei?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let H be a many-body Hamiltonian acting on an A-fermion Hilbert space, and let S be a class of "simple" intrinsic states Φ (for example, Slater determinants or Hartree–Bogoliubov quasiparticle vacua) on this space. For Φ ∈ S, let ρ_Φ(x) denote the one-body density associated with Φ. For each triple of angular-momentum labels (J, M, K) with |M|, |K| ≤ J, let P^J_{MK} denote the standard angular-momentum projection operator built from rotation operators R(Ω) and Wigner D-functions, so that Φ_{JMK} := P^J_{MK} Φ is a state of definite total angular momentum J and projection M (with intrinsic projection K).

Define the projected energy
  E[Φ; J, M, K] := ⟨Φ_{JMK}| H |Φ_{JMK}⟩ / ⟨Φ_{JMK}|Φ_{JMK}⟩,
and define the intrinsic-density functional
  F_{JMK}[ρ] := inf { E[Φ; J, M, K] : Φ ∈ S, ρ_Φ = ρ },
with associated minimum E_{JMK} := inf_ρ F_{JMK}[ρ]. A priori F_{JMK}[ρ] depends on the class S and on the labels (J, M, K).

(a) Determine sufficient conditions on the Hamiltonian H, the class S, and the range of labels (J, M, K) under which there exists a single density ρ* (or a single intrinsic state Φ* ∈ S) that is, to a controlled approximation, a minimizer of F_{JMK}[·] simultaneously for a large family of values of (J, M, K), so that one intrinsic density ρ* serves as a common minimizer for many projected rotational states Φ_{JMK}.

(b) Establish a precise relationship between such an intrinsic-density functional F_{JMK}[ρ] and the standard three-dimensional energy density functionals E[ρ] employed for deformed many-body systems, in which the deformed (intrinsic) density is treated as the fundamental variable without explicit angular-momentum projection.
artifact.status_search_result: The question concerns the foundations of projected/intrinsic-density functional theory for deformed nuclei. The literature on multi-reference and projected EDFs (e.g., works by Duguet, Bender, Lacroix and collaborators) discusses partial results and self-consistency issues, but no general theorem characterizing when one intrinsic density can serve a large family of (J,M,K) projected states, nor a rigorous derivation linking such a functional to standard 3D deformed EDFs, has been established. The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Open Problems in Nuclear Density Functional Theory
status_evidence.snippet: Lists conceptual open problems in nuclear DFT including the status of intrinsic/rotational density functionals.
status_evidence.claim: The problem is posed as an open problem in nuclear DFT.

status_evidence.title: Particle-number restoration within the energy density functional formalism
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses pathologies and foundational issues with projected EDFs, indicating the lack of a fully rigorous framework.
status_evidence.claim: Foundational issues with projected/intrinsic EDFs remain unresolved.
